**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 22 already sits at our preferred position on every parameter the rule tracks:

| Parameter | Preferred position | Document (§22) |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | ≤1 per 12 months | Once in any twelve-month period ✓ |
| Notice | 30 days' written | Thirty days' prior written ✓ |
| Timing | Business hours | Normal business hours, no unreasonable disruption ✓ |
| Auditor | Independent, confidentiality-bound | Independent auditor bound by confidentiality ✓ |
| Location | Off-site where possible | Off-site where practicable ✓ |
| Cost | Vendor's, unless underpayment >5% | Vendor bears, shifts only above five percent ✓ |
| System access | None | Express bar on direct system access ✓ |

Two points worth noting beyond the checklist:

- **§22.3 gives us more than the playbook asks for** — audit findings are our Confidential Information, usable only to enforce the Agreement; Vendor must hand over the final report; and paying a shortfall closes out the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error. Nothing here needs defending.
- **The planner's flagged risk did not materialise.** Section 23 is titled "RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE" but contains only the heading with no operative text, so it creates no second, unbounded audit channel. A full-text sweep for audit/inspect/verify/monitor/records/examine/assurance turned up no other clause imposing verification duties on us. §22.2's carve-out also usefully protects privileged material and other suppliers' confidential information.

One drafting observation I did *not* redline, since it falls outside this rule and is not adverse to us: the empty Section 23 heading is likely a residual artifact. It is harmless as drafted, but if Copperleaf later proposes filling it in, that text should be re-tested against this rule — an assurance or records right dropped there could bypass the §22 limits entirely.
